title: 2003 AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: The sum of three numbers is \(20.\) The first is \(4\) times the sum of the other two. The second is seven times the third. What is the product of all three?

solutions.text:
Let the numbers be \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c.\) Since \(a = 4(b + c),\) we get \(4(b + c) + (b + c) = 20,\) so \(b + c = 4\) and \(a = 16.\)

With \(b = 7c,\) we have \(7c + c = 4,\) so \(c = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(b = \dfrac{7}{2}.\)

The product is \(16 \cdot \dfrac{7}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = 28.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the third number be \(c;\) then the second is \(7c\)
The first number equals \(4(b + c),\) so \(4(b + c) + (b + c) = 20\)
